candidates.source_name: Úřad práce ČR (ÚP ČR) — statistics portal, incl. mass-redundancy notifications
candidates.why_relevant: Employers must notify the regional ÚP branch of hromadné propouštění under the Labour Code (§62, employers with 20+ staff). ÚP has historically issued press releases and regional/annual reports counting notifications, affected headcount and sector breakdown — i.e. the legally-forced disclosure of downsizing that firms do not announce. Note: the site moved to the up.gov.cz domain in Feb 2026 (old uradprace.cz / mpsv.cz/up-cz paths may redirect).
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Monthly crawl of regional statistics pages and PDF reports; extract mass-redundancy notification counts; keyword-filter for NACE K / finance. Confirm current URL paths after the domain migration.
candidates.discovered_via_method: local-language search on the legal notification term

negative_findings.description: Searched in Czech for a public, itemised register of hromadné propouštění notifications naming the employer. Úřad práce ČR publishes counts and sector breakdowns (press releases, regional annual reports, open data), but I found no evidence of a public per-employer notification register.
negative_findings.result_summary: Aggregate-only disclosure found; per-employer notifications appear not to be published, only aggregated (e.g. '15 notifications, up to 831 employees' in a month, with sector groupings like energy, clothing, machinery).
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Means firm-level detection of a Czech bank's collective redundancy must come from unions, media or ad-hoc ÚP/regional statements — the statutory notification itself is not a directly harvestable source. Consider an Info Act (zákon č. 106/1999 Sb.) request as a collection method.

negative_findings.description: Searched in Czech for works councils (rada zaměstnanců) and European Works Councils (evropská rada zaměstnanců) specifically in Czech banks. Only generic legal/explanatory material was found (Labour Code Part 12, ČMKOS guide PDF, MPSV handbook, academic theses).
negative_findings.result_summary: No public register or directory of which Czech banks have a rada zaměstnanců or which are covered by an EWC of their foreign parent (Erste, KBC, Société Générale, UniCredit, Raiffeisen).
negative_findings.why_it_matters: EWC-level consultation is where group-wide offshoring/restructuring affecting the Czech subsidiary is first disclosed. Absent a register, coverage must be inferred from parent-group union federations (UNI Europa Finance) and from parent annual/sustainability reports.

negative_findings.description: OSPPP publishes the existence of a higher-level collective agreement (Kolektivní smlouva vyššího stupně, KSVS 2022-2025) in its documents section, but firm-level collective agreements at individual banks were not found publicly.
negative_findings.result_summary: Only the sector-level KSVS is publicly referenced; per-bank kolektivní smlouvy are not published.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Firm-level agreements contain redundancy severance multiples and job-security clauses — high-value org-change intelligence that is only obtainable via the union or leaked/reported summaries. Also: the KSVS end-date 2022-2025 suggests a successor agreement should exist and be tracked.

negative_findings.description: Úřad práce ČR moved its web presence to up.gov.cz in February 2026; historical links live under uradprace.cz and mpsv.cz/up-cz.
negative_findings.result_summary: Three coexisting host patterns observed in search results for the same statistical pages.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: A collector built on old paths will produce false 'dead source' verdicts. All ÚP URLs in this slice should be treated as unverified until a deterministic liveness pass resolves the current canonical host.

coverage_gaps.description: No per-bank union organisation website or newsletter was located for the big three (Česká spořitelna, ČSOB, Komerční banka). ZO entities are confirmed to exist as registered legal persons (multiple IČOs each) and OSPPP has per-employer subpages, but their own communication channels (intranet-only in many cases) were not found.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Snowball from https://www.osppp.cz/nase-sluzby/odborove-organizace to enumerate every per-employer subpage; search each ZO name plus 'zpravodaj'/'informace pro členy'; check Facebook groups. Consider direct contact with OSPPP for public statements.

coverage_gaps.description: This slice is bank-heavy. Payments-specific employers (payment institutions, card processors, fintechs, shared-service/offshoring centres run by banking groups in Brno/Ostrava) were not separately searched for workforce/union coverage.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run Czech queries on 'centrum sdílených služeb banka Brno propouštění', 'platební instituce zaměstnanci', 'back office banky Ostrava rušení' and check CzechInvest/regional development agency announcements of finance-sector service-centre openings and closures.

coverage_gaps.description: No FOI-style collection path was tested. The Czech Freedom of Information Act (zákon č. 106/1999 Sb.) could compel Úřad práce ČR to disclose mass-redundancy notifications by NACE sector and possibly by employer.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Pilot a written 106/1999 request to ÚP ČR for mass-redundancy notifications in CZ-NACE section K over the last 36 months; treat as a recurring quarterly request if fruitful.

coverage_gaps.description: English-language coverage of this cell is thin and mostly EU-level (Eurofound ERM, UNI Europa). No Czech-based English-language outlet covering bank labour disputes was identified.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Test Expats.cz, Czech Radio International (english.radio.cz) and CTK/ČTK English wire for finance-sector layoff coverage.

coverage_gaps.description: ČNB branch-count data was confirmed to exist and be cited by media, but the exact ARAD time-series identifier for branch / business-place counts was not pinned down in this pass.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Navigate the ČNB ARAD database explicitly to locate the series for 'počet poboček' / 'obchodní místa' and record the stable series code and export endpoint.

brief: Workforce-level org change in Czech banking is legible through three distinct layers. First, the union layer is unusually concentrated: a single sector union, OSPPP (member of ČMKOS), covers ~150 basic organisations across 27+ banks and insurers, publishes a higher-level collective agreement, and is the actor that reliably makes downsizing visible — its firm-level ZO entities are individually registered in the public registry, giving a clean actor map. Second, the statutory layer (Labour Code mass-redundancy notification to Úřad práce ČR, plus mandatory consultation with the union or works council) generates a paper trail, but ÚP publishes only aggregates and sector groupings, so firm-level detection depends on unions, regional Deník reporting, or a 106/1999 Sb. information request. Third, the statistical layer — ČSÚ NACE-K employment and wages, ISPV occupational earnings, and ČNB branch/business-place counts, with Peníze.cz maintaining a usable per-bank branch-count series and Eurofound ERM logging ≥100-job Czech events — lets contraction be measured even when nobody announces it.
